# Embedded, automotive, and industrial

Applies when the change touches: firmware, vehicles, OT. Every role loads this pack for the steps it works in, on top of its own playbook. The test commands below are best practices the gate runs: put them in the Spec's `[[tests.commands]]`, so a red one blocks the merge. Name the pack in the Spec's Context; it does not count against a Task's `skills`.

## Standards

| Standard | Edition | Checked | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MISRA C or MISRA C++ | MISRA C:2025 and MISRA C++:2023, which absorbs AUTOSAR C++14 | 2026-09-28 | <https://misra.org.uk/> |
| ISO 26262 and ISO/SAE 21434 | 26262:2018, 21434:2021 | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.iso.org/standard/68383.html> |
| IEC 61508 | 2010 | 2026-09-28 | <https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/5515> |
| IEC 62443 | series, with 62443-4-1:2018 and 62443-4-2:2019 | 2026-09-28 | <https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/33615> |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item |
| --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd next`) | Safety-related code is major with the security pool; name the safety integrity level (ASIL, SIL) the change touches. |
| Specify | Requirements trace to tests; timing, memory, and power budgets in the Acceptance; failure modes and safe states named. |
| Implement | MISRA-compliant code with documented deviations; no dynamic allocation after init where the standard forbids it; secure boot and update paths untouched or re-verified. |
| Review | Static analysis clean; hardware-in-the-loop or simulation results for the changed behavior. |
| Ship | Staged fleet rollout with a rollback image; fault and reset telemetry as the observe signals. |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MISRA and static analysis | no rule violation without a documented deviation | Cppcheck with the MISRA addon, Clang-Tidy, or a qualified tool |
| Coverage at the required level | statement, branch, or MC/DC coverage as the standard requires | the unit test runner with coverage thresholds |
| HIL or simulation run | the changed behavior holds on hardware or a model | the HIL rig or simulator in CI |
| Firmware signing test | an unsigned or tampered image is rejected | a test of the update path |
| Fuzzing | every parser and protocol handler survives malformed input | libFuzzer or AFL++ on the handlers |

## Keep it current

A standard marked emerging is a draft, a first edition, or a young practice: apply it only when the change clearly needs it, and say so in the Spec. A standard checked more than a year ago is stale: `aidd eval standards` lists it, and the loop contract's research-first rule applies. When the change needs a standard this pack lacks, look up the authoritative source, record the edition in the Spec's Context, and propose the update to the aidd project's roles registry (`schemas/roles.json` in the aidd repository) as an improvement.
